rows.citation: White NJ. Anaemia and malaria. Malar J. 2018;17(1):371. PMID 30340592. doi:10.1186/s12936-018-2509-9.
rows.proposition: Malaria can produce clinically significant anemia through hemolysis of infected and uninfected erythrocytes and impaired erythropoiesis; the relationship is strongest when anemia is temporally linked to active or recent malaria.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: separately documented anemia temporally compatible with active or recent malaria
rows.guard: Require established malaria and a separately documented anemia phenotype with compatible timing. Do not infer chronic anemia from remote resolved malaria. Preserve nutritional deficiency, blood loss, hemoglobinopathy, chronic kidney disease, marrow disease, hemolysis from other causes, and other competing etiologies.
rows.scopeFinding: The review directly identifies malaria as a major cause of anemia and describes hemolysis of infected and uninfected erythrocytes plus marrow dyserythropoiesis. The implemented chronology and competing-cause guard is appropriately narrower than the population-level review.

rows.sourceTitle: Human immunodeficiency virus-related peripheral neuropathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.citation: Julian T, Rekatsina M, Shafique F, Zis P. Human immunodeficiency virus-related peripheral neuropathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Neurol. 2021;28(4):1420-1431. PMID 33226721. doi:10.1111/ene.14656.
rows.proposition: HIV/AIDS is associated with a distinct spectrum of peripheral neuropathies, especially distal predominantly sensory polyneuropathy, through HIV disease mechanisms and, in some patients, treatment-related neurotoxicity.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: separately diagnosed HIV-related peripheral neuropathy, including distal predominantly sensory polyneuropathy
rows.guard: Require established HIV/AIDS and a separately diagnosed peripheral-neuropathy phenotype. Distinguish HIV-related disease mechanisms from antiretroviral neurotoxicity and preserve diabetes, alcohol, nutritional deficiency, chemotherapy, compressive neuropathy, opportunistic infection, and other neurologic causes.
rows.scopeFinding: The systematic review directly supports HIV-related peripheral neuropathy, identifies distal predominantly sensory polyneuropathy as the commonest phenotype, and recognizes primary HIV, opportunistic/inflammatory mechanisms, and ART adverse effects. The implementation correctly separates disease and treatment mechanisms and preserves competing causes.

rows.sourceTitle: Anemia as the Main Manifestation of Myelodysplastic Syndromes
rows.citation: Santini V. Anemia as the Main Manifestation of Myelodysplastic Syndromes. Semin Hematol. 2015;52(4):348-356. PMID 26404446. doi:10.1053/j.seminhematol.2015.06.002.
rows.proposition: Anemia is a major clinical manifestation of myelodysplastic syndromes and may arise from ineffective/dysplastic erythropoiesis.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: separately documented anemia in established myelodysplastic syndrome
rows.guard: Require established myelodysplastic syndrome and separately documented anemia. Do not attribute every anemia automatically to MDS; preserve bleeding, iron/B12/folate deficiency, chronic kidney disease, hemolysis, treatment effects, inflammatory disease, and other marrow disorders.
rows.scopeFinding: The review states that MDS shares anemia in the great majority of cases and explains ineffective erythropoiesis as a central mechanism. The implementation remains appropriately diagnosis-specific and requires independent documentation of anemia and competing-cause review.

rows.sourceTitle: Primary myelofibrosis: update on definition, pathogenesis, and treatment

rows.proposition: Anemia is a recognized clinical hallmark of primary myelofibrosis in the setting of marrow fibrosis and disordered hematopoiesis.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: separately documented anemia in established primary myelofibrosis
rows.guard: Require established primary myelofibrosis and separately documented anemia. Preserve bleeding, nutritional deficiency, renal disease, hemolysis, treatment effects, coexisting marrow disease, and leukemic transformation as competing or contributing explanations.
rows.scopeFinding: The review explicitly lists anemia among the clinical hallmarks of primary myelofibrosis. The existing implementation does not overstate individual causation and appropriately preserves alternative and contributing causes of anemia.

rows.sourceTitle: Chronic renal insufficiency in heart transplant recipients: risk factors and management options
rows.citation: González-Vílchez F, Vázquez de Prada JA. Chronic renal insufficiency in heart transplant recipients: risk factors and management options. Drugs. 2014;74(13):1481-1494. PMID 25134671. doi:10.1007/s40265-014-0274-9.
rows.proposition: Chronic kidney disease is a recognized post-heart-transplant complication, with calcineurin-inhibitor nephrotoxicity acting within a multifactorial post-transplant risk model.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: separately established chronic kidney disease arising after actual heart transplantation with compatible chronology
rows.guard: Require an actual heart transplant and separately established post-transplant chronic kidney disease with compatible chronology. Do not infer CKD from transplant status alone. Preserve preexisting CKD, diabetes, hypertension, perioperative acute kidney injury, cardiorenal/hemodynamic factors, rejection-related injury, and other nephrotoxic exposures.
rows.scopeFinding: The review directly describes renal dysfunction after heart transplantation as frequent and explicitly characterizes chronic kidney disease as multifactorial, with calcineurin-inhibitor nephrotoxicity acting on a predisposed recipient. The implementation already contains the necessary actual-transplant, chronology, and competing-cause restrictions.
